BiblicalUsage: The word appears once, in the law of Ahasuerus's feast: 'the drinking was according to the law; none did compel: for so the king had appointed to all the officers of his house, that they should do according to every man's pleasure.' In a palace where the king's word was law, this once the drinking was not forced — every man drank as he pleased.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for compelling carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the small mercy in the feast — even in a pagan king's house, no one was forced to drink.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
